notes:
Rules for solving inequalities

  • Adding/subtracting the same number to both sides preserves the inequality direction.
  • Multiplying/dividing both sides by a positive number preserves the direction; by a negative number reverses it.
  • Taking reciprocals of both (same-sign) sides reverses the inequality: if $a 1/b$.

Algebraic (one variable)

  • Solve like an equation but flip the sign when multiplying/dividing by a negative.
  • Solution of $ax+b < 0$ ($a>0$): $x < -b/a$; represented on number line with open circle (strict) or closed circle ($\le,\ge$).
  • Compound inequality $a < px+q < b$: solve both parts, take intersection.

Modulus inequalities

InequalitySolution
$|x| < a$ ($a>0$)$-a
$|x| > a$ ($a>0$)$x<-a$ or $x>a$
$|x| \le a$$-a\le x\le a$

Graphical solution of a system in two variables

  • A linear inequality $ax+by \le c$ divides the plane into two half-planes by the line $ax+by=c$; the solution region is one half-plane (test with origin if it does not lie on the line).
  • Solid line for $\le, \ge$ (boundary included); dashed line for $<, >$ (boundary excluded).
  • The feasible region of a system is the intersection of all individual half-planes (common shaded region), often a bounded/unbounded polygon.

Word problems

  • Translate 'at least' as $\ge$, 'at most' as $\le$, 'more than' as $>$, 'less than' as $<$.

Exam tip

KCET typically asks 1 question from this chapter, usually on solving a linear inequality in one variable or identifying the correct graphical region for a system of two inequalities. The most common trap is forgetting to flip the inequality sign when multiplying/dividing by a negative number.

questions.q: The solution set of $3x - 5 < 7$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$ is
questions.explanation: $3x < 12 \Rightarrow x < 4$.
questions.trick: Isolate $x$ like an equation; no negative multiply here, sign stays.

questions.q: The solution set of $-2x + 3 \ge 7$ is
questions.explanation: $-2x \ge 4 \Rightarrow x \le -2$ (sign flips on dividing by $-2$).
questions.trick: Dividing by a negative number flips the inequality sign.

questions.q: If $x$ is a natural number and $2x+1 < 10$, the solution set is
questions.explanation: $2x < 9 \Rightarrow x < 4.5$; natural numbers satisfying this: $1,2,3,4$.
questions.trick: Solve for $x$, then keep only the natural numbers in range.

questions.q: The solution of $|x-2| < 3$ is
questions.explanation: $|x-2|<3 \Rightarrow -3<x-2<3 \Rightarrow -1<x<5$.
questions.trick: $|x-a|<r \Rightarrow a-r<x<a+r$.

questions.q: The solution of $|2x+1| \ge 5$ is
questions.explanation: $2x+1 \ge 5 \Rightarrow x\ge2$, or $2x+1\le-5 \Rightarrow x\le-3$.
questions.trick: $|x-a|\ge r \Rightarrow x\le a-r$ or $x\ge a+r$.

questions.q: The compound inequality $-3 < 2x - 1 \le 5$ has solution
questions.explanation: Add 1: $-2 < 2x \le 6$; divide by 2: $-1 < x \le 3$.
questions.trick: Apply the same operation to all three parts of the compound inequality together.

questions.q: The graph of $x + y \le 4$ in the $xy$-plane is
options: a half-plane not containing the origin
a half-plane below (and including) the line $x+y=4$, containing the origin
questions.explanation: Testing origin $(0,0)$: $0 \le 4$ is true, so the origin's side (below the line) is the solution region, boundary included since $\le$.
questions.trick: Test the origin in the inequality to find which half-plane it's in.

questions.q: For $a<b$ with $a,b$ both negative, which is true?
questions.explanation: For same-sign numbers, taking reciprocals reverses the inequality: $a<b \Rightarrow 1/a>1/b$ (e.g. $a=-3,b=-1$: $1/a=-1/3 > 1/b=-1$).
questions.trick: Same-sign reciprocals flip the inequality direction.

questions.q: If $x$ and $y$ are real numbers satisfying $2x+3y > 6$, the point $(0,0)$
questions.explanation: Substituting $(0,0)$: $2(0)+3(0)=0>6$ is false, so the origin does not satisfy the inequality.
questions.trick: Plug $(0,0)$ straight into the inequality and check if it holds.

questions.q: The solution set of $\dfrac{x-2}{3} \ge \dfrac{x-1}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 6: $2(x-2) \ge 3(x-1) \Rightarrow 2x-4 \ge 3x-3 \Rightarrow -1 \ge x \Rightarrow x\le-1$.
questions.trick: Clear denominators by multiplying by their LCM (a positive number) first.

questions.q: A student needs at least 40 marks out of 50 to pass. If $x$ denotes marks scored, this is represented as
questions.explanation: 'At least 40' means marks must be 40 or more, i.e. $x \ge 40$.
questions.trick: 'At least' translates to $\ge$.

questions.q: The solution set of the system $x \ge 0, y \ge 0, x+y \le 5$ represents
options: a bounded triangular region in the first quadrant
questions.explanation: $x\ge0,y\ge0$ restricts to the first quadrant; $x+y\le5$ cuts off a triangle with vertices $(0,0),(5,0),(0,5)$ — a bounded region.
questions.trick: $x,y\ge0$ pins the region to quadrant I; add the line to bound it.

questions.q: If $-4x \ge 12$, then
questions.explanation: Dividing by $-4$ (negative) flips the sign: $x \le -3$.
questions.trick: Dividing by a negative coefficient flips the inequality.

questions.q: The values of $x$ satisfying both $x > -2$ and $x < 5$ simultaneously are represented as
questions.explanation: Taking the intersection ('and') of both conditions gives $-2 < x < 5$.
questions.trick: 'And' of two conditions means take their intersection on the number line.

questions.q: The solution of $5x - 3 < 3x + 1$ is
questions.explanation: $5x-3x < 1+3 \Rightarrow 2x < 4 \Rightarrow x < 2$.
questions.trick: Collect $x$ terms on one side, constants on the other; sign unchanged (positive divide).

questions.q: If temperature in Celsius $C$ satisfies $30 \le C \le 40$, the corresponding Fahrenheit range using $F = \dfrac{9}{5}C + 32$ is
questions.trick: Plug both endpoints of $C$ into the linear formula to get the $F$ range.

questions.q: Which point lies in the solution region of $x - y \le 1$ and $x + y \ge 3$?
questions.explanation: Check $(2,2)$: $x-y=0\le1$ true; $x+y=4\ge3$ true. Both satisfied, so $(2,2)$ is in the solution region.
questions.trick: Test each option point directly in both inequalities.

questions.q: The inequality $|x| \le 0$ has solution set
questions.explanation: $|x| \ge 0$ always, so $|x|\le0$ forces $|x|=0$, giving the single solution $x=0$.
questions.trick: $|x|\ge0$ always, so $|x|\le0$ forces $x=0$ only.

questions.q: If $2 \le 3x-4 \le 11$, the range of $x$ is
questions.explanation: Add 4: $6 \le 3x \le 15$; divide by 3: $2 \le x \le 5$.
questions.trick: Undo operations on all three parts together: add, then divide.

questions.q: The maximum number of pens a shopkeeper can buy at ₹8 each with a budget of at most ₹100 is represented by which inequality (n = number of pens)?
questions.explanation: 'At most ₹100' spent means total cost $8n$ must satisfy $8n \le 100$, giving $n \le 12.5$, so at most 12 pens.
questions.trick: 'At most' translates to $\le$; solve then floor to a whole number.

questions.q: The solution of $\dfrac{2x+1}{3} < 5$ is
questions.explanation: $2x+1<15 \Rightarrow 2x<14 \Rightarrow x<7$.
questions.trick: Clear the fraction by multiplying (positive), then isolate $x$.

questions.q: The solution of $3x+2 > x-4$ is
questions.explanation: $3x+2>x-4 \Rightarrow 2x>-6 \Rightarrow x>-3$.
questions.trick: Move all $x$ to one side, constants to the other, sign unchanged.

questions.q: The number of integers satisfying $-3 \le x < 2$ is
questions.explanation: The integers are $-3,-2,-1,0,1$, which is 5 integers ($2$ itself is excluded).
questions.trick: List integers between the bounds; upper end excluded if strict.

questions.q: The largest natural number satisfying $2x - 3 < 7$ is
questions.explanation: $2x<10 \Rightarrow x<5$; the largest natural number less than 5 is 4.
questions.trick: Solve the inequality, then pick the largest integer strictly below the bound.

questions.q: The solution of $|x+3| > 5$ is
questions.trick: $|x-a|>r \Rightarrow x>a+r$ or $x<a-r$.

questions.q: The general solution of $|x| > a$ (where $a>0$) is
questions.explanation: $|x|>a$ means $x$ lies outside $[-a,a]$, i.e. $x<-a$ or $x>a$.
questions.trick: $|x|>a \Rightarrow x<-a$ or $x>a$ — outside the interval.

questions.q: The solution of $-5x + 10 \le 0$ is
questions.explanation: $-5x \le -10$; dividing by $-5$ flips the inequality: $x \ge 2$.
questions.trick: Dividing by a negative coefficient flips the inequality sign.

questions.q: The graph of $x \ge 2$ in the $xy$-plane represents
options: the region to the right of (and including) the vertical line $x=2$
the region to the left of $x=2$
questions.explanation: $x\ge2$ includes the vertical line $x=2$ and every point with $x$-coordinate at least 2, i.e. the region to its right.
questions.trick: $x\ge k$ is everything to the right of the vertical line $x=k$.

questions.q: The graph of $y < 3$ in the $xy$-plane represents
options: the region to the right of $x=3$
the region below the horizontal line $y=3$, excluding the line
questions.explanation: $y<3$ is a strict inequality, so it is the open half-plane below the dashed line $y=3$.
questions.trick: Strict inequality $\Rightarrow$ open (dashed) boundary, region excludes the line.

questions.q: The solution of $\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{x}{3} < 5$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{3x+2x}{6}<5 \Rightarrow \dfrac{5x}{6}<5 \Rightarrow x<6$.
questions.trick: Clear fractions via LCM (positive), then isolate $x$.

questions.q: If $a > b$ and $c < 0$, then
questions.explanation: Multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses it, so $a>b$ gives $ac<bc$ when $c<0$.
questions.trick: Multiplying by a negative $c$ flips $>$ to $<$.

questions.q: The solution of $7 \le \dfrac{3x+11}{2} \le 11$ is
questions.explanation: Multiply by 2: $14 \le 3x+11 \le 22$; subtract 11: $3\le 3x\le 11$; divide by 3: $1\le x\le\dfrac{11}{3}$.
questions.trick: Undo in reverse order across all three parts: multiply, subtract, divide.

questions.q: A student scored 62 in one test. For the average of this and a second test score $x$ to be at least 70, $x$ must satisfy
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{62+x}{2}\ge70 \Rightarrow 62+x\ge140 \Rightarrow x\ge78$.
questions.trick: Average $\ge$ target $\Rightarrow$ sum $\ge$ target$\times$count; solve for $x$.

questions.q: The solution of $4(x-2) \ge 2(x+3)$ is
questions.explanation: $4x-8\ge2x+6 \Rightarrow 2x\ge14 \Rightarrow x\ge7$.
questions.trick: Expand both sides first, then collect $x$ terms — positive divide keeps sign.

questions.q: The solution set of $x<3$ and $x>3$ holding simultaneously is
questions.explanation: No real number can be both strictly less than 3 and strictly greater than 3, so the solution set is empty.
questions.trick: No number can be both $<3$ and $>3$ — the answer is always the empty set.

questions.q: Which of the following values of $x$ does NOT satisfy $-2 < x \le 5$?
questions.explanation: The inequality is strict at $-2$ (excluded), so $x=-2$ does not satisfy it, while $0$, $3$ and $5$ all do.
questions.trick: Check the strict/non-strict boundary carefully — endpoints matter.

questions.q: The solution set of $|x-1| \le 4$ is
questions.explanation: $|x-1|\le4 \Rightarrow -4\le x-1\le4 \Rightarrow -3\le x\le5$.
questions.trick: $|x-a|\le r \Rightarrow a-r\le x\le a+r$.

questions.q: The region satisfying $x\ge0, y\ge0, x\le4, y\le3$ is a
questions.explanation: The four inequalities bound $x$ between 0 and 4 and $y$ between 0 and 3, giving a rectangle with vertices $(0,0),(4,0),(4,3),(0,3)$.
questions.trick: Two-sided bounds on $x$ and $y$ separately give a rectangle.

questions.q: The solution of $6x - 3 \ge 4x + 5$ is
questions.explanation: $6x-3\ge4x+5 \Rightarrow 2x\ge8 \Rightarrow x\ge4$.
questions.trick: Collect $x$ terms on one side; positive coefficient keeps the sign.

questions.q: A taxi charges ₹50 plus ₹12 per km. If a passenger has at most ₹200 to spend, the maximum whole number of km they can travel is
questions.explanation: $50+12x\le200 \Rightarrow 12x\le150 \Rightarrow x\le12.5$; the largest whole number of km is 12.
questions.trick: Set up cost $\le$ budget, solve, then floor to a whole number.
